prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Time for Common Sense: a government that trusts people, not politicians. Conservatives will set individuals, families, professionals and entrepreneurs free—while cherishing the institutions, communities and national traditions that bind us together.

- Raising a family: Back marriage and family responsibility. Cut taxes for parents of young children by boosting the Children’s Tax Credit; restore a new Married Couple’s Allowance worth up to £1,000 via transferable allowances; reform Working Families Tax Credit so payment goes to the caring parent; abolish tax on Widowed Parent benefits; offer Family Scholarships to help parents re‑skill. In schools, create Free Schools: real autonomy for heads and governors, less bureaucracy, discipline restored (easy exclusion of disruptors; Progress Centres), successful schools free to expand, new faith/parent/charitable schools allowed, and a Parent’s Guarantee to trigger Ofsted and change failing management. Students repay loans only above £20,000; no top‑up fees. Endow universities for independence.

- Living safely: More police, less paperwork; “cops in shops” visibility; parish constables. Tenfold expansion of Secure Training Centre places; mandatory prison for dealers selling to under‑16s; aggravated sentences near schools. Honesty in sentencing—criminals serve what courts impose; end automatic early release. Prisoners to work and pay towards victims and families. Lifetime supervision available for sex offenders; protect children online. Put victims first with named contacts and fair self‑defence law.

- Earning a living: A tax‑cutting, deregulating government. Save £8bn versus Labour’s plans and return it in targeted cuts: abolish tax on most savings and dividends; raise pensioners’ Personal Allowance by £2,000; restore married couple support; cut petrol/diesel duty by at least 6p; scrap IR35; reduce business rates and reward enterprise. Simpler, more transparent taxes; a National Accounts Commission. Regulatory budgets to cut burdens yearly; exempt small firms from some rules. Scrap the Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear; focus regulators on competition. Keep the pound; veto further power transfers to Brussels; spending to grow within trend growth; strengthen BoE independence and external fiscal scrutiny.

- Staying healthy: Match NHS funding plans but end political meddling. Abolish the Waiting List Initiative; introduce a Patient’s Guarantee—maximum waits set by clinical need, with a right to be treated elsewhere (NHS or independent) if breached. Restore ward authority (bring back Matron); expand practice nurses; fund stand‑alone surgical units; create an Exceptional Medicines Fund; increase hospice funding; end tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable. Choice for patients and GPs.

- Growing older: Respect and independence, not means‑testing. Raise the basic state pension, with higher uprating for over‑75s; allow optional consolidation of extras into a higher tax‑free pension; lift a million pensioners out of tax; abolish compulsory annuitisation at 75; move toward funded pensions for the young; protect prudent savers from long‑term care confiscation.

- Knowing who we are—a world leader: In Europe, not run by Europe. Keep the pound and the veto; renegotiate Nice; embed reserved powers at home; complete the single market; cut EU waste. Strong defence in NATO; no EU army outside NATO; end political correctness in the forces and exempt them from ECHR; support US ballistic missile defence; maintain our nuclear deterrent. Be a safe haven, not a soft touch on asylum: secure reception centres, fast decisions, safe‑country rule, and a Removals Agency.

- A stronger society: Build civic strength, not state dependency. Create an Office of Civil Society; cut charity VAT using euro‑prep funds; replace New Deal with Britain Works (pay by sustained jobs); Can Work, Must Work; fairer savings rules and faster rehab for disabled people; a national anti‑fraud squad and NI cleanup.

- Town & Country: Foot & Mouth Recovery Strategy now. Cut rural business rates; protect post offices with a secure benefit card; scrap top‑down housebuilding targets; new “Blue Belts” for waterways; cut fuel duty; fair deal for farmers (honest labelling, CAP and CFP reform). Regenerate cities via local Regeneration Companies; more policing, Partner Schools, brownfield first, stronger Right‑to‑Buy, rent‑to‑mortgage.

- A civilised country: Free culture from state control—privatise Channel 4 and endow arts with £3bn; back tourism; simplify media rules; a single communications regulator; fair, independent BBC regulation; boost school and grassroots sport.

- A proud democracy: Power down to effective local councils and local referendums on big tax hikes; scrap regional quangos; English votes for English laws; strengthen Lords via independent appointments and pursue lasting reform; tougher parliamentary scrutiny; fewer ministers, MPs and spin doctors.

Time to deliver. Time for common sense.
